newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends mixed, Dec sets new contract low.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends mixed, Dec sets new contract low.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended mixed on bear-spreading, but traders said strength in CBOT wheat helped limit losses.

KCBT Dec wheat set a new contract low at $3.97-1/2 but settled at $3.99-1/2, down 1-1/2 cents on the day. That marked the first time a nearby KCBT wheat contract has closed below $4.00 since December, 1994.
Overall, KCBT wheat settled 1-1/2 cents per bushel lower to 1-1/2 cents higher.
Traders said the tone for KCBT wheat was set early when Refco sold one million Dec bushels.
"After that, we saw some bear-spreading and also I think some intermarket spreads. People who had bought (KCBT wheat) versus Chicago got out of those positions," a trader said.
KCBT Dec wheat also sagged as Gulf basis bids eased by about five cents, traders said.

Apart from Refco's sale of one million Dec bushels early , Wolcott Lincoln bear-spread one million March/Dec at 18-1/2 cents. FIMAT and LFG also bear-spread 500,000 March/Dec each at 18-1/2 cents. Prudential bought one million March bushels.
Early weakness in U.S. wheat markets came after the Australian Wheat Board upped its estimate of Australian wheat production to 21 million tonnes, from the previous estimate of 20 million.
